leads.name: The Railway Poplar, Alexandra Park
leads.species: Railway Poplar (likely Populus x canadensis, historic cultivar), Alexandra Park
leads.location_hint: Alexandra Park, Whalley Range, Manchester M16 8HZ
leads.reason: Named by the council's RHS/Owen Johnson survey page as 'one of the biggest in England', alongside the Variegated Green Ash which shipped as mcr_004 from the same park. Not used this pass under the four-candidate limit and because only one source (the council page) was found for either; the Ash was chosen as the fourth candidate since it carries a documented planting period. Worth its own pass if a second source turns up, since 'one of the biggest in England' is a strong claim.

leads.location_hint: Fog Lane Park, Fog Lane, Didsbury, Manchester M20 6HG
leads.reason: Named by the council's RHS/Owen Johnson survey page as 'some of the tallest in England', in the same park as the Crimean Limes that shipped as mcr_005. Only one source found. Not pursued further under the four-candidate limit.

leads.name: Scotch Laburnum, Fog Lane Park
leads.location_hint: Fog Lane Park, Fog Lane, Didsbury, Manchester M20 6HG
leads.reason: Named by the council's RHS/Owen Johnson survey page as 'one of the tallest in England', in the same park as mcr_005. Only one source found. Not pursued further under the four-candidate limit.

leads.name: Northern Catalpa, Fog Lane Park
leads.location_hint: Fog Lane Park, Fog Lane, Didsbury, Manchester M20 6HG
leads.reason: Named by the council's RHS/Owen Johnson survey page with no superlative attached (just listed). Only one source found, no distinguishing detail beyond presence. Weakest of the Fog Lane candidates; not pursued.

leads.name: Silver Birch 'Golden Cloud', Fletcher Moss Botanical Gardens
leads.location_hint: Fletcher Moss Botanical Garden, Stenner Lane, Didsbury, Manchester M20 2RQ
leads.reason: Named by the council's RHS/Owen Johnson survey page as 'a very rare tree'. Only one source found; not pursued this pass since Fletcher Moss already contributed two trees (mcr_002, mcr_003).

leads.name: Eucalyptus, Heaton Park
leads.reason: Named by the council's RHS/Owen Johnson survey page as 'might be the biggest of its species' (hedged, not a confirmed claim). Only one source, and the hedge itself makes it a weaker claim than the other council-page trees. Heaton Park otherwise returned no single named, dated, individually-remarkable tree in general web research this pass (see below); this Eucalyptus is the one specific lead the council page gives for that park.

leads.name: Cappadocian Maple, Parsonage Gardens
leads.location_hint: Parsonage Gardens, Stenner Lane, Didsbury (opposite St James' Church, adjoining Fletcher Moss Botanical Garden)
leads.reason: Only source found across both passes is monumentaltrees.com (girth 2.06m, estimated 126 +/- 30 years old as of 2024), which per hard rule 1 may verify but never be the sole source. The council's rare-trees page (checked this second pass) does not mention this tree, so it did not gain a source. Still needs one independent source before it can ship.

leads.name: The Manchester Poplar, St John's Gardens
leads.location_hint: St John's Gardens, Lower Byrom Street/Byrom Street/Quay Street, Castlefield, Manchester (a former churchyard, redeveloped as a public garden in 1932)
leads.reason: A second, younger Manchester Poplar specimen distinct from mcr_001 (Annie Lees Park, Gorton). Confirmed to exist by Wikipedia's St John's Gardens article and a 2014 city-centre tree trail piece, but neither gives an age, girth or planting date, and the garden itself only dates from 1932. Recorded as a lead rather than blocked in case a future pass finds it is more storied than the 1932 redevelopment suggests.

leads.name: Heaton Park veteran trees (unnamed, other than the Eucalyptus lead above)
leads.species: unknown; the park's own descriptions mention a Turkey Oak (Quercus cerris) and 'some of the oldest trees in the park' surviving in the restored Western Pleasure Ground, no individual named or dated
leads.location_hint: Heaton Park, Prestwich/Higher Blackley, Manchester, especially the Western Pleasure Ground near Heaton Hall
leads.reason: Historic England's Register entry (list-entry/1000854) 403s to curl; not retried via browser this pass since the four-candidate slots were spent on the council page's Fletcher Moss/Alexandra Park/Fog Lane trees instead. Worth a dedicated pass with browser access, same as the council page turned out to be.

leads.name: St Mary's Church, Didsbury churchyard tree
leads.reason: No source found across two passes naming any specific old or notable tree at this churchyard. Not blocked, just unresearched.

leads.name: Blackley churchyard tree (St Peter's or other)
leads.location_hint: St Peter's Church, Old Market Street, Blackley, Manchester (built 1844) or another Blackley churchyard
leads.reason: No source found across two passes naming any specific old or notable tree here. St Peter's itself only dates from 1844, capping how old any planted specimen could plausibly be unless it predates the current building on an older church site. Not blocked, just unresearched.
